provenance.sourceOrg: Indiana Election Division, Office of the Secretary of State
provenance.quote: Currently, under the Constitution of the State of Indiana, a person charged with murder or treason is not entitled to be released on bail if the proof is evident or the presumption strong. Shall the Constitution of the State of Indiana be amended to provide that a person charged with an offense other than murder or treason is not entitled to bail if: (1) the proof is evident or the presumption strong; and (2) the state proves by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions will reasonably protect the safety of any other person or the community. (This question concerns Article 1, Section 17 of the Constitution of the State of Indiana.)

provenance.sourceOrg: Indiana Election Division, Office of the Secretary of State
provenance.quote: Shall the Constitution of the State of Indiana be amended to permit the judge of a city or town court to reside in: (1) the county in which the court is located; or (2) the bordering county closest to the city or town in which the court is located? (This question concerns Article 6, Section 6 of the Constitution of the State of Indiana.)

measures.questionText: Currently, under the Constitution of the State of Indiana, a person charged with murder or treason is not entitled to be released on bail if the proof is evident or the presumption strong. Shall the Constitution of the State of Indiana be amended to provide that a person charged with an offense other than murder or treason is not entitled to bail if: (1) the proof is evident or the presumption strong; and (2) the state proves by clear and convincing evidence that no release conditions will reasonably protect the safety of any other person or the community. (This question concerns Article 1, Section 17 of the Constitution of the State of Indiana.)

provenance.sourceOrg: Indiana Election Division, Office of the Secretary of State

measures.questionText: Shall the Constitution of the State of Indiana be amended to permit the judge of a city or town court to reside in: (1) the county in which the court is located; or (2) the bordering county closest to the city or town in which the court is located? coverageNotes: The Indiana Election Division publishes its 2026 General Election Candidate List for all counties. All 137 federal, statewide and state legislative contests and 271 listed candidates were converted from that workbook, including declared write-in candidates. The list provides no incumbency or campaign website fields.

The official workbook provides the full candidate list for each saved contest. The Election Division’s August 2026 newsletter cautions about ballot-name spellings: “Please do not rely on spellings that you might find on websites—even our candidate list posted to the IED website! The certification documents are the ballot names provided by the candidates and reviewed by staff.” https://www.in.gov/dA/fdebb4ee35/Dispatch.Aug-2026.FINAL.pdf?language_id=1

The Election Division’s August 2026 newsletter states that two state constitutional amendment questions will be certified to counties. Both exact questions were converted from its 2026 election legislation summary and matched to Hamilton County’s official November 3, 2026 sample ballot. The county’s local Public Question #3 was excluded because it applies only to Carmel Clay Schools.

Both public questions link to their official General Assembly resolution pages: Senate Enrolled Joint Resolution 1 (2026) and House Enrolled Joint Resolution 1 (2025). The exact links were read from the Indiana Senate and House Republican Caucuses’ public legislative articles. Both resolution pages returned HTTP 200 with their JavaScript application shell; their full amendment texts are linked and were not extracted.

The official Court of Appeals districts page states: Judges representing the 4th and 5th districts stand for retention statewide. Judges named from these districts stand for retention only in their districts. The county ballot’s Second District retention is outside the requested statewide-office scope and was excluded.

Indiana’s Fall 2026 election reminder states that the federal-only ballot includes only United States Representative. No U.S. Senate contest is on the 2026 general ballot. https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/files/Fall%202026%20Clerks%20Meetings.FINAL.pptx
